new_statements.quote: 2.1.2. Тональные противопоставления не обнаружены. Ударение динамически-тоновое, разноместное. Место ударения в слове зависит от фонетических и морфологических факторов. В большинстве словоформ ударение стоит на ближайшем к концу слова долгом гласном, а при отсутствии в непрерывных [sic, printed thus; sense requires 'непервых'] слогах долгих гласных — на гласном первого слога (pu·rqɨ 'дым', ūčɨqo 'работать', aqqɔ̄·l 'вожжа', ūčɔ̄·mɨt 'мы работаем', ɔtäqɨlɨ· 'ваши два оленя'). Имеются, кроме того, два класса аффиксов, из которых одни перетягивают на себя ударение в нарушение указанного правила (koŋa·ltɨqo 'рассказать', pūto·ntɨ 'внутрь'), а другие создают двуударность словоформ (tɨ̄·lɔ̄· 'поближе сюда', tɛ·nɨsɨ·mil' 'умный').
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Tonal oppositions have not been found. Stress is dynamic-tonal and free [non-fixed in position]. The place of stress in a word depends on phonetic and morphological factors. In most word forms the stress falls on the long vowel nearest the end of the word, and, when there are no long vowels in non-initial syllables, on the vowel of the first syllable (pu·rqɨ 'smoke', ūčɨqo 'to work', aqqɔ̄·l 'rein', ūčɔ̄·mɨt 'we work', ɔtäqɨlɨ· 'your two reindeer'). There are, in addition, two classes of affixes: some pull the stress onto themselves in violation of the stated rule (koŋa·ltɨqo 'to tell', pūto·ntɨ 'inside'), others create double-stressed word forms (tɨ̄·lɔ̄· 'closer, hither', tɛ·nɨsɨ·mil' 'clever').

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Selkup (src qs-tier-2026-09-12) has an empty rule string and there are no existing_statements, so this supplies the placement rule rather than confirming or contradicting one: rightmost long vowel, else initial, with affix-driven exceptions and double stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No tone. Stress is quantity-sensitive and mobile: it falls on the rightmost long vowel of the word; if no non-initial syllable has a long vowel, on the first syllable (default-to-initial). Two lexically marked affix classes override this: one attracts stress to itself, the other yields two stresses in one word form. Because stress depends on morpheme composition it can distinguish word forms (kɨ·kɨtil' 'loving' vs kɨkɨ·til' 'riverless'; čɛ·lčalqo 'to trample' vs čɛlča·lqo 'to stamp').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as secondary stress as such; the source speaks of 'двуударность' (double stress) in word forms carrying certain affixes, e.g. tɨ̄·lɔ̄· 'closer, hither', tɛ·nɨsɨ·mil' 'clever'.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) Affix class that attracts stress against the long-vowel rule (koŋa·ltɨqo 'to tell', pūto·ntɨ 'inside'); (b) affix class producing double stress; (c) dialectal: 'Для некоторых диалектов характерна тенденция к перетяжке ударения на краткие нередуцированные гласные непервого слога, особенно на широкие a, ä (центр. kana·k 'собака', äwä· 'мать')' = in some dialects (central examples given) stress tends to shift to short non-reduced non-initial vowels, especially the open vowels a, ä; (d) apparent stress-based minimal pairs arise from differing morphemic composition.
new_statements.identity_note: Khelimsky 1993 describes Selkup as a whole with a Northern (Taz) base and explicit dialect notes: the drift of stress onto short non-reduced non-initial a/ä is attributed to 'некоторые диалекты' with central-dialect examples (kana·k 'dog', äwä· 'mother'). The 2018 Kazakevich article (the item the open_url actually resolves to) transcribes a Northern Selkup shamanic song from the Krasnoselkup district (YaNAO) and says nothing about stress.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the OchSJa 1980:138-141 block quote is verbatim in the held Normanskaja 2018 txt at pp.270-271, and the p.222 paraphrase is there too; the primary itself is not yet obtained. (2) Deciding source is the 1980 MGU reference grammar of Taz Selkup (Glottolog 'grammar', 424 pp), carried second-hand. I downloaded the open publisher PDF of Jazyki mira: Ural'skie jazyki (1993) and read Helimski's Selkup chapter: §2.1.2 p.358 states first-hand the same rule — stress on the long vowel nearest the word end, else on the first-syllable vowel, plus stress-attracting and double-stress affix classes — which confirms classification weight, heavy=CVV (long vowel), edge=unbounded, default initial, and the the secondary-stress rule note on double-stressed forms. It also adds a dialect note (central dialects shift stress onto short open non-first vowels) consistent with Normanskaja's finding that southern/central Selkup differs. (3)

sources.citation: Inkelas, Sharon & Wilbanks, Eric. 2018. Directionality effects via distance-based penalty scaling. Proceedings of the Annual Meetings on Phonology 5 (AMP 2017): 11 pp. doi:10.3765/amp.v5i0.4256
sources.quote: A similar case of conflicting directionality in another domain is Selkup stress. In this system, as described by Zoll (1997), rightmost heavy syllables receive stress. However, if there are no heavy syllables, the leftmost light syllable receives stress. This behavior is exemplified in (1). (1) Selkup stress examples from Halle & Clements (1983) a. /u:"cO:m1t/ 'we work' (rightmost heavy) b. /"karman/ 'pocket' (leftmost light)
sources.note: Theoretical OT/HG paper on distance-based penalty scaling that analyses Selkup stress assignment as an 'opposite-edge' directionality case alongside Ngore-Kiga harmony, Japanese mimetics and Macedonian stress windows.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meetings on Phonology

sources.citation: Zoll, Cheryl. 1997. Conflicting directionality. Phonology 14(2): 263-286. doi:10.1017/s0952675797003369
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: Descriptively, in Selkup the rightmost heavy (CVV) syllable receives the stress (1), but if the word contains no heavy syllables, it is the leftmost syllable which is stressed (2). The term conflicting directionality describes this elsewhere relationship between the right and left edges of a word.
sources.locator: p. 1 (printed page of the ROA-151 manuscript; sec. 1 Introduction); data sets (1)-(2) p. 1-2 and repeated as (40)-(41) p. 29, both headed 'Data from Halle and…
sources.note: The abstract states the Selkup stress rule: stress falls on the rightmost heavy (CVV) syllable, and on the leftmost syllable when the word has no heavy syllable, a pattern the paper calls conflicting directionality. The catalog entry has classification weight with an empty rule; the abstract supplies the rule statement (rightmost heavy, default leftmost) and cites Halle & Clements 1983 and Idsardi 1992 as its data sources, with no phonetic measurement.
